payout_quote: New York's Returnable Container Act, more commonly referred to as the "Bottle Bill," requires a deposit of at least 5-cents on carbonated soft drinks, beer and other malt beverages, mineral water, soda water, wine products (wine coolers) and water that doesn't contain sugar. / Consumers may then return their empty beverage containers to a retailer or redemption center to get their deposit back.
steps: Buy eligible NY-deposit beverages in New York (5¢ deposit at checkout)
Keep empty containers with the NY refund label, empty and intact
Return them to any dealer selling the same brand/type/size or to a redemption center (any hour except first/last hour of dealer's day)
Receive the 5¢-per-container refund in cash, no proof of purchase needed
catches: This returns YOUR OWN deposit money paid at purchase — it is recovering your own money, not new income.
Only containers bought in-state with the correct deposit label are redeemable; out-of-state containers are ineligible and redeeming them is fraud.
Dealers may limit returns to 240 containers/day (72 for small stores); returning containers you did not pay a NY deposit on is illegal.
biggest_catch: Returns your own 5¢ deposit — you paid it at purchase. This is deposit recovery, not income.
eligibility: Anyone who purchased NY-deposit containers in New York State.
timing: Refund paid in cash at return.

c1.evidence: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) Bottle Bill page; dec.ny.gov.

c2.evidence: Official DEC page: deposit of at least 5 cents; consumers return empties to a retailer or redemption center to get their deposit back.

c3.evidence: No fee; deposit already paid at purchase.

c4.evidence: 5¢ cash refund per container; NYC311 confirms stores must accept containers for refund.

s1.note: NY-purchased, NY-labeled eligible containers; empty and intact.

s6.note: Steps are concrete: buy, save, return to dealer/redemption center, get cash.

notes: NYC311 page independently confirms the 5¢ refund right at any retailer selling beverages.
numeric_basis: payout from official DEC terms (5¢/container); time: collecting empties + return trip est. 20–60 min active.
